beats.hindi_tts: Traditional envelopes place fixed percentage bands, like 3% or 5%, above and below the moving average.
beats.en_subtitle: Traditional envelopes place fixed percentage bands, like 3% or 5%, above and below the moving average.

leftColumn.title: Moving Average Envelopes
leftColumn.subtitle: Fixed Percentage Channels
bullets: Bands set at fixed distance (e.g. ±3% or ±5%)
Captures roughly 85-90% of price swings
Major flaw: Cannot adjust to sudden market volatility

rightColumn.title: Bollinger Bands
rightColumn.subtitle: Dynamic Volatility Standard Deviations
bullets: Middle line: 20-day Simple Moving Average
Bands placed at ±2 Standard Deviations (2σ)
Automatically expands in turmoil, contracts in calm

beats.en_narration: Traditional envelopes place fixed percentage bands, like 3% or 5%, above and below the moving average.

beats.hindi_tts: John Bollinger integrated statistical standard deviation, allowing the bands to breathe with volatility.

leftColumn.title: Static Envelopes
leftColumn.subtitle: Rigid Boundaries
bullets: Breached constantly in high volatility crises
Price never reaches bands in quiet consolidations

rightColumn.title: Bollinger Bands Advantage
rightColumn.subtitle: Adaptive Self-Scaling Channels
bullets: Encompasses ~95% of all price observations
Eliminates need for manual percentage recalibration
Bands act as relative overbought/oversold gauges

leftColumn.title: Donchian Entry Rule
leftColumn.subtitle: Pure 20-Day / 4-Week Channel Breakout
bullets: Cover shorts and go Long whenever price exceeds highest high of past 4 calendar weeks
Liquidate longs and go Short whenever price drops below lowest low of past 4 calendar weeks
Completely objective, mechanical, and 100% trend-following

rightColumn.title: Risk & Whipsaw Reality
rightColumn.subtitle: The Price Paid for Megatrends
bullets: Generates heavy whipsaws in consolidation ranges
Win-rate often sits around 35-40%
Profits on outsized trends far eclipse small losses

beats.hindi_tts: Perry Kaufman solved the rigid parameter dilemma: a moving average that automatically adapts to market speed.
beats.en_subtitle: Perry Kaufman solved the rigid parameter dilemma: a moving average that automatically adapts to market speed.

leftColumn.title: Kaufman Adaptive MA (KAMA)
leftColumn.subtitle: Efficiency Ratio Driven
bullets: Measures Efficiency Ratio (ER) = Directional Price Change / Total Volatility Path
In a smooth vertical trend (ER ≈ 1), it speeds up like a 2-day fast EMA
In choppy noisy chop (ER ≈ 0), it slows down to a 30-day sluggish flat line

rightColumn.title: Standard Static MA
rightColumn.subtitle: Blind Rigid Speed
bullets: Moving at same speed regardless of market noise
Trapped in constant whipsaws during consolidations
Lags behind fast explosive momentum moves

ui_state.question: A stock's Bollinger Band Width hits its lowest value in 12 months. Price then breaks above the upper band on surging volume. Does touching the upper band mean it is overbought and should be shorted?
ui_state.answer: NO! An extreme low in Band Width signals 'The Squeeze'. Breaking the upper band on heavy volume signals trend initiation, not an overbought top. Prices routinely 'walk the band' during powerful momentum runs.
